findings.dependency_and_impact: Section 3.3 explicitly makes the comparison of generalization frameworks part of the paper's explanation and directs readers to Appendix C and Table 1. The false inequality is the quantitative link offered for the fat-shattering certificate in that comparison. Its failure invalidates that technical component of the central comparison, independently of the separate countable-hypothesis proof. Appendix location does not remove that dependency.

alternatives_counterevidence: Not a reproduction of the nonlinear data in Figure1
findings.dependency_and_impact: The abstract and introduction advertise simple model examples and soft inductive bias as core contributions. Section 2 designates this polynomial as the running example, derives the exact low-degree preference from its penalty, and Sections 4/7 reuse this construction to explain generalization behavior. The counterexample breaks that claimed optimizer-selection step in the core example. Severity does not require the broad soft-bias idea, empirical curves, or the independent countable bound to fail.
